### How to try activities 1–6

1. Read **Your task**, then edit the sample response or enter your own. Some
   sample responses contain deliberate beginner mistakes.
2. Choose **Feedback**. On a first visit, **Copy prompt** mode shows a prompt to
   paste into your chosen AI chat.
3. For a reply on this page, open the **⚙ Feedback settings** cogwheel, select
   **Direct API**, and enter your institution's base URL, model and personal key.
   Their cogwheels open the same settings, shared across this website. Saved
   settings are reused on later visits.

For image activities, choose a model that accepts images. In **Copy prompt** mode,
attach the original image separately in your AI chat. In **Direct API** mode, your
response, selected source/context and uploaded images go to the configured
provider. Images are kept in memory, not saved in browser storage.

### 1. Beginner Spanish writing

::: {.callout-note .example-author-notes}
### For course authors

**Feature:** a plain textarea activity, without a checker or Python runtime.
The `language-quality` profile reviews Spanish at the author-defined level
"Spanish course 1" and explains improvements in English. The starting text
contains verb-agreement mistakes; learners may edit it or write their own text.
`context="none"` keeps these demonstration notes out of the prompt.
:::

::: {.ai-feedback #spanish-writing profile="language-quality" response-language="es" feedback-language="en" learner-level="Spanish course 1" context="none"}
**Your task**

Write three to five simple Spanish sentences about where you live and what you
do in the morning. Use the draft below as a starting point, or replace it with
your own text. Choose **Feedback** when you are ready for advice in English.

::: {.feedback-criteria}
Review vocabulary and present-tense grammar appropriate to Spanish
course 1.
:::

::: {.feedback-criteria}
Suggest up to three useful improvements while preserving the learner's
meaning and simple style; do not replace the whole response.
:::

::: {.feedback-starter}
Yo vive en Trondheim. Cada mañana yo come pan y bebo café.
:::
:::

### 2. English to Spanish translation

::: {.callout-note .example-author-notes}
### For course authors

**Feature:** an original text nested inside the activity as `.feedback-source`.
The `translation` profile receives the English source separately from the
Spanish response and gives feedback in English. The starting translation is
valid: try changing a detail to see how meaning and grammar are reviewed.
:::

::: {.ai-feedback #translation profile="translation" source-language="en" response-language="es" feedback-language="en" learner-level="Spanish course 1" context="none"}
**Your task**

Translate the English text below into Spanish using simple language. Review the
draft in the response field, or replace it with your own translation, then
choose **Feedback** for advice in English.

::: {.feedback-source}
Every morning, Maria walks to school with her brother. They like studying languages.
:::

::: {.feedback-starter}
Cada mañana, María camina a la escuela con su hermano. Les gusta estudiar idiomas.
:::
:::

### 3. Spanish adjective agreement

::: {.callout-note .example-author-notes}
### For course authors

**Feature:** a reusable lesson block selected with `context="agreement"`.
The legacy `.math-exercise-context` class works for language learning too;
`.ai-feedback-context` and `.ai-context` are aliases. Only the tagged lesson is
included as context. The interface stays in English, while feedback is in
Norwegian Bokmål.
:::

**Lesson reminder**

::: {#agreement .math-exercise-context}
An adjective agrees in gender and number with the noun it describes.
:::

::: {.ai-feedback #context-alias profile="language-quality" response-language="es" feedback-language="nb" learner-level="Spanish course 1" context="agreement"}
**Your task**

Write one Spanish sentence describing two red houses. Use the lesson reminder
above to check your adjective endings. Edit the draft, then choose **Feedback**;
the explanation will be in Norwegian Bokmål.

::: {.feedback-starter}
Las casas son rojo.
:::
:::

### 4. Feedback on handwritten Spanish

::: {.callout-note .example-author-notes}
### For course authors

**Feature:** `image-upload="true" image-role="response"` treats an uploaded image
as the learner's work, so typed text is optional. Use a vision-capable model for
direct feedback. The downloadable, AI-generated handwriting sample contains
two deliberate beginner mistakes for testing; feedback wording will vary by model.

To test image reading, leave **Your response** empty. Look for feedback on the
verb forms in the second and third sentences. The sample is not attached automatically.
:::

::: {.ai-feedback #handwriting profile="language-quality" response-language="es" feedback-language="en" learner-level="Spanish course 1" image-upload="true" image-role="response" context="none"}
**Your task**

Write three short Spanish sentences introducing yourself, saying where you live,
and mentioning something you like. Photograph your handwriting and select the
photo with **Upload images**, or use the sample below to try the activity.
You may leave **Your response** empty. Choose **Feedback** for advice in English.

[Download the Spanish handwriting sample (PNG)](assets/spanish-handwriting.png){#handwriting-sample-download download="spanish-handwriting.png"}
Save the image, then select it with **Upload images**.

::: {.feedback-criteria}
Read the handwritten Spanish and identify up to three useful
improvements to vocabulary, grammar or spelling at Spanish course 1 level. If a
word is unreadable, say so instead of guessing. Do not rewrite the whole response.
:::
:::

### 5. Describe a picture in Spanish

::: {.callout-note .example-author-notes}
### For course authors

**Feature:** `image-role="source"` makes the picture supporting material, while
the typed Spanish description is the response being reviewed. Unlike the
handwriting activity, an image alone is not a learner response. Try a photo of a
room or a landscape and use a vision-capable model for direct feedback.
:::

::: {.ai-feedback #describe-picture profile="language-quality" response-language="es" feedback-language="en" learner-level="Spanish course 1" image-upload="true" image-role="source" context="none"}
**Your task**

Upload a picture of a room or a landscape. In **Your response**, write three simple
Spanish sentences describing things you can see in it. Choose **Feedback** for
advice in English about your Spanish and how well the description fits the picture.

::: {.feedback-criteria}
Review vocabulary and grammar appropriate to Spanish course 1, and
whether the description matches the visible picture. Do not invent details that
cannot be seen, and do not supply a complete replacement description.
:::
:::

### 6. German to Norwegian on an English page

::: {.callout-note .example-author-notes}
### For course authors

**Feature:** independent source, response and feedback languages. This page and
its interface are English; the original is German, the response is Norwegian
Bokmål, and the feedback is English. The reusable source block is marked
`.ai-context`. The activity gives it its role with `source="german-original"`.
`context="none"` excludes these notes without removing the explicit source.
The draft includes an unnatural time expression for the learner to improve.
:::

**Original text — German**

::: {#german-original .ai-context}
Am Samstag fährt Lena mit dem Zug nach Oslo. Sie besucht ihre Schwester,
die seit zwei Jahren dort wohnt. Wenn das Wetter gut ist, gehen sie am
Nachmittag am Hafen spazieren. Am Sonntag fährt Lena wieder nach Hause.
:::

::: {.ai-feedback #german-to-norwegian profile="translation" source="german-original" source-language="de" response-language="nb" feedback-language="en" context="none"}
**Your task**

Translate the German passage above into Norwegian Bokmål. Edit the draft below,
or replace it with your own translation. Choose **Feedback** for advice in
English about meaning, natural Norwegian phrasing and grammar.

::: {.feedback-criteria}
Preserve the German meaning, tense, relationships and sequence
of events. Accept valid alternative Norwegian Bokmål translations. Explain up to
three improvements in English, quoting German or Norwegian where useful. Do not
supply a complete replacement translation.
:::

::: {.feedback-starter}
På lørdag reiser Lena med tog til Oslo. Hun besøker søsteren sin, som bor der
siden to år. Hvis været er fint, går de en tur ved havnen på ettermiddagen.
På søndag reiser Lena hjem igjen.
:::
:::
